To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a minimal regulatory network of extrinsic and intrinsic factors recovers observed patterns of CD4+ cell differentiation and plasticity.

a minimal regulatory network model of CD4+T cells, derived from experimental data, recovers most of the reported cell types and plasticity transitions, and that this model suggests that the micro-environment plays a key role in these transitions.
a minimal Boolean regulatory model derived from experimental data can recover the reported configurations of the characterized cell-types and the observed plastic responses of CD4+T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic regulation of CD4+T cells and the role of the micro-environment in their differentiation and plasticity.
the development of a mathematical framework for modeling and understanding the complex dynamics of CD4+ cells.
the development and validation of an in silico model of the CD4+ T helper cell system, and the use of this model to study the mechanisms of plasticity of this important immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the minimal regulatory network is sufficient to recover most of the observed CD4 T cell types and their transitions.
the observed plastic CD4+ T responses can be recovered by a minimal network model that integrates transcriptional regulation with signaling pathways and the extrinsic environment.
the intrinsic and extrinsic components are tightly coupled and the observed CD4 T-cell types and transitions emerge from their interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a minimal network model of the core transcription factors and signaling pathways involved in CD4 T cell-fate acquisition can recover the reported patterns of cell types and transitions.
the observed CD4 + T cell-types and transitions emerge from the feedback of the intrinsic or intracelluar regulatory core and the extrinsic or extracelluar regulatory microenvironment.

the observed CD4 ^{+} T cell-types and their transition patterns emerge from a minimal regulatory core that is robust to perturbations, but is also sensitive to transient activations and inhibitions of the extrinsic factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a small number of core factors and a few micro-environmental factors can explain most of the observed plasticity patterns.
the observed plastic responses of CD4+ lymphocytes are the result of a minimal core network that is robust to perturbations.

the observed plasticity and fate of CD4+T cells is the result of an intricate interplay between extrinsic factors and intrinsic factors, which are themselves the result of a complex regulatory network.
